text: Puella dominum videt.
translation: The girl sees the master.

text: Miles bellum amat.
translation: The soldier loves the war.

text: Bona puella hunc dominum videt.
translation: The good girl sees this master.

text: Puella bona est.
translation: The girl is good.

text: Magnus miles parvam puellam videt.
translation: The great soldier sees the small girl.

text: Ille dominus eam amat.
translation: That master loves her.

text: Ipse dominus novum bellum videt.
translation: The master himself sees the new war.

text: Is puellam amat.
translation: He loves the girl.

text: Dominus militem regit.
translation: The master rules the soldier.

text: Miles dominum capit.
translation: The soldier captures the master.

text: Puella dominum audit.
translation: The girl hears the master.

text: Miles urbem regit.
translation: The soldier rules the city.

text: Dominus civem videt.
translation: The master sees the citizen.

text: Miles mare videt.
translation: The soldier sees the sea.

text: Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres, quarum unam incolunt Belgae.
translation: All Gaul is divided into three parts, one of which the Belgae inhabit.

text: Si hortum in bibliotheca habes, nihil deerit.
translation: If you have a garden in your library, nothing will be lacking.

text: Consul, cum in senatum venisset, cives monuit ut urbem defenderent.
translation: When the consul had come into the senate, he warned the citizens to defend the city.

text: Hostibus victis, imperator militibus praemia promissa dedit.
translation: The enemies having been conquered, the commander gave the promised rewards to the soldiers.

text: Nemo tam stultus est ut libenter periculo se committat.
translation: No one is so foolish that he would willingly commit himself to danger.

text: Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes.
translation: I fear the Greeks, even when bringing gifts.

text: Multi credunt nos feliciores futuros esse si divitias magnas habeamus.
translation: Many believe that we will be happier if we should have great wealth.

text: Pueris rogantibus quid accidisset, magister veritatem celare non potuit.
translation: When the boys asked what had happened, the teacher could not hide the truth.

text: Rex legem bonam populo dicit.
translation: The king speaks a good law to the people.

text: Pater filium in domum ducit.
translation: The father leads the son into the house.

text: Vir fortis magnum ignem timet.
translation: The brave man fears a large fire.

text: Femina epistulam fratri scribit.
translation: The woman writes a letter to her brother.

text: Milites aciem in monte ponunt.
translation: The soldiers place the battle line on the mountain.

text: Nox noctem sequitur et dies diem.
translation: Night follows night and day follows day.

text: Civis de salute pacis quaerit.
translation: The citizen inquires concerning the safety of peace.

text: Amicus pecuniam sine mora mittit.
translation: The friend sends money without delay.

text: Nullum periculum animum verum movet.
translation: No danger moves a true mind.

text: Auctoritas ducis legioni spem dat.
translation: The authority of the leader gives hope to the legion.

text: Post tempestatem nautae navem in flumine inveniunt.
translation: After the storm the sailors find the ship in the river.

text: Poeta de vita et morte in terra docet.
translation: The poet teaches about life and death on the earth.

text: Dux audax exercitum per agros agit.
translation: The bold leader drives the army through the fields.

text: Saepe stulti fortunam et famam quaerunt.
translation: Often foolish people seek fortune and fame.

text: Semper veritatem scire volumus.
translation: We always want to know the truth.

text: Gravis dolor mentem et corpus movet.
translation: Heavy grief affects the mind and the body.

text: Totus populus pacem ab imperatore petit.
translation: The whole people seeks peace from the commander.

text: Legatus solus ad urbem altam pervenit.
translation: The envoy arrives alone at the high city.

text: Pater putat filium magistrum intellegere.
translation: The father thinks that the son understands the teacher.

text: Milites ex castris exire coguntur.
translation: The soldiers are compelled to go out of the camp.

text: Homines in aede deos colunt et pacem petunt.
translation: Humans worship the gods in the temple and seek peace.

text: Imperator equos et copias sub monte manere iubet.
translation: The commander orders the horses and troops to remain under the mountain.

text: Dux agmen per longam viam ducit sed hostes tela iaciunt.
translation: The leader leads the column along the long road but the enemies hurl weapons.

text: Postquam rex orationem habuit, pauci cives de eius fide dubitaverunt.
translation: After the king gave a speech, few citizens doubted his loyalty.

text: Nunc autem amor et amicitia mentem meam tenent.
translation: Now however love and friendship hold my mind.

text: Miles acer in loco aequo stat et officium facit.
translation: The keen soldier stands in a fair place and does his duty.

text: Pater suum filium ad se vocat ne malum casum patiatur.
translation: The father calls his own son to himself lest he suffer a bad accident.

text: Consul dicit se ius et potestatem habere.
translation: The consul says that he has right and power.

text: Ante lucem exercitus magnitudine sua hostes vicit.
translation: Before dawn the army conquered the enemy by its greatness.

text: Idem homo fessus laborem ferre debet.
translation: The same tired man ought to bear the labor.

text: Inter cives nox finem curae et dolori dat.
translation: Among the citizens night gives an end to care and grief.

text: Aetas et tempus omnia facta cognoscunt.
translation: Age and time recognize all deeds.

text: Cornu altius in caelo ab aliquo videtur.
translation: A horn is seen higher in the sky by someone.

text: Poeta audeat novum opus pro patria gerere.
translation: Let the poet dare to undertake a new work for the fatherland.
